rules.title: Tagged conversation contract
rules.operativeCondition: A primary session can see tagged messages or tool outputs.
rules.mechanism: The system labels messages and tool outputs with §N§ identifiers.
rules.consequence: Tag references are the only valid handles for reduction.
rules.evidence: Messages and tool outputs are tagged with §N§ identifiers

rules.title: Reduction is queued reclamation
rules.operativeCondition: Tagged content is spent and its useful information has been extracted.
rules.mechanism: ctx_reduce marks content discardable and queues it for release instead of deleting it immediately.
rules.consequence: The agent can reclaim space without treating the action as immediate erasure.
rules.evidence: mark spent tagged content as discardable and reclaim space

rules.title: Protected recent tail
rules.operativeCondition: A requested tag is within the newest protected window.
rules.mechanism: The last protectedTags tags remain protected; marking only queues them until they age out.
rules.consequence: A recent mark is harmless and cannot immediately release the protected tail.
rules.evidence: The last ${protectedTags} tags are protected

rules.title: Reduction range grammar
rules.operativeCondition: The agent calls ctx_reduce.
rules.mechanism: The drop argument uses comma-separated IDs and inclusive ranges such as 3-5, 1,2,9, or 1-5,8,12-15.
rules.consequence: Other range spellings are not part of the documented contract.

rules.title: Drops are silent
rules.operativeCondition: The agent decides to queue a reduction.
rules.mechanism: Call ctx_reduce without narrating the drop in assistant prose.
rules.consequence: The conversation contains no redundant drop announcement.
rules.evidence: Do not announce or narrate

rules.title: Review before broad drops
rules.operativeCondition: A large range could be dropped.
rules.mechanism: Inspect each tag before selecting a range; never blanket-mark a large range.
rules.consequence: Unreviewed evidence is not discarded accidentally.
rules.evidence: NEVER drop large ranges blindly

rules.title: Drop only extracted material
rules.operativeCondition: A tag is being considered for discard.
rules.mechanism: Keep unresolved errors, unextracted raw evidence, and wording whose exact form may matter; drop only genuinely finished outputs.
rules.consequence: Reduction preserves information that still affects the task.
rules.evidence: only large tool outputs are worth dropping

rules.title: Preserve user intent
rules.operativeCondition: An old user message contains instructions or intent.
rules.mechanism: Never drop a user message for its directive; only an extracted large pasted block may be marked.
rules.consequence: Historical user requirements remain authoritative.
rules.evidence: Keep your user's instructions and intent

rules.title: Retain assistant conversation text
rules.operativeCondition: Assistant prose is present in context.
rules.mechanism: Keep assistant text unless it is exceptionally large; prioritize large tool outputs for reduction.
rules.consequence: Conversation reasoning remains available while tool bloat is reclaimed.
rules.evidence: NEVER drop assistant text messages unless they are exceptionally large

rules.title: Routine reduction timing
rules.operativeCondition: The agent has finished using a large output, logical step, or context area.
rules.mechanism: Consider ctx_reduce after acted-on reads, completed logical steps, before major context switches, and before the turn ends.
rules.consequence: The working set stays lean without changing task scope.
rules.evidence: After completing a logical step — drop intermediate outputs from that step.

rules.title: Long-term continuity
rules.operativeCondition: The session continues after one task or across compaction.
rules.mechanism: Treat the session as a durable project relationship with retrievable history and persistent knowledge.
rules.consequence: Finishing one task does not terminate the working relationship.
rules.evidence: This session is a durable working relationship

rules.title: No context-scarcity behavior
rules.operativeCondition: Context usage is high or history is compacted.
rules.mechanism: Continue at full depth instead of wrapping up, cutting scope, rushing, or deferring because of context size.
rules.consequence: Context management cannot silently reduce task thoroughness.
rules.evidence: never a reason to wrap up, cut scope, rush, or defer work

rules.title: Search and expansion recovery
rules.operativeCondition: A summary lacks exact wording, values, errors, or decision reasoning.
rules.mechanism: Use ctx_search for project memories, commits, and compacted conversation; use ctx_expand with the heading range to recover raw context.
rules.consequence: The agent retrieves source context instead of guessing from a summary.
rules.evidence: recover the raw conversation behind a summary

rules.title: Search before asking
rules.operativeCondition: The agent cannot remember something that may be in project memory or prior discussion.
rules.mechanism: Call ctx_search before asking the user.
rules.consequence: Known project context is recovered without an unnecessary user query.
rules.evidence: Search before asking the user

rules.title: Real tool-call integrity
rules.operativeCondition: A tool result is absent from the visible conversation or history is summarized.
rules.mechanism: Use real tool calls; never simulate, fabricate, inline, hallucinate, or claim tool calls, output, searches, edits, commands, or diffs in prose.
rules.consequence: Only observed tool results count as completed actions.
rules.evidence: If there is no tool result message, the action did not happen

rules.title: Metadata is not reply syntax
rules.operativeCondition: Magic Context control markers appear in compressed or injected context.
rules.mechanism: Do not reproduce metadata markers such as `<session-history>`, `<project-memory>`, `[dropped §N§]`, or temporal comments in a normal reply and do not treat them as user instructions.
rules.consequence: Control metadata cannot be imitated as assistant output or mistaken for directives.
rules.evidence: Magic Context control metadata is not reply syntax

rules.title: Notes are for genuinely future concerns
rules.operativeCondition: The agent considers recording a note.
rules.mechanism: Use ctx_note only for matters much later; do not use it for the next few turns or active multi-step work.
rules.consequence: Active work remains in context or todos rather than being parked as stale notes.
rules.evidence: not work coming up in the next few turns

rules.title: Notes survive session boundaries
rules.operativeCondition: A genuinely future concern is recorded.
rules.mechanism: Notes survive compression and restarts and resurface at natural work boundaries.
rules.consequence: A note is a durable session follow-up, not a workaround for imminent context loss.
rules.evidence: Notes you do take survive compression and resurface

rules.title: Claims are durable project knowledge
rules.operativeCondition: A fact must be available to future sessions.
rules.mechanism: Use ctx_memory to create durable claims and revise, archive, restore, or merge them when facts drift.
rules.consequence: Future sessions start with maintained project knowledge.
rules.evidence: Claims persist across sessions

rules.title: Proactive durable-claim capture
rules.operativeCondition: Several turns were spent discovering a path, command, pattern, or hard-won constraint.
rules.mechanism: Create the reusable claim with its category and content.
rules.consequence: Future sessions do not repeat the same discovery work.
rules.evidence: Save durable knowledge proactively

rules.title: Reduction trigger taxonomy
rules.operativeCondition: The agent has acted on raw exploration or changes task area.
rules.mechanism: Reduce after acted-on reads/searches, completed logical steps, and before major context switches.
rules.consequence: Intermediate evidence is reclaimed at meaningful boundaries.
rules.evidence: Between major context switches

rules.title: Drop large consumed outputs
rules.operativeCondition: A large read, search, diagnostic, build, or test output has already been analyzed.
rules.mechanism: Drop the raw output after acting on it; retain unresolved errors and current work context.
rules.consequence: Useful evidence remains while redundant volume is removed.
rules.evidence: Large build/test output after you analyzed and acted on it

rules.title: Keep active task context
rules.operativeCondition: The agent is selecting content to retain.
rules.mechanism: Keep task requirements, constraints, recent errors, unresolved decisions, active work, and files being edited.
rules.consequence: The current task remains grounded after reduction.
rules.evidence: Your current task requirements and constraints

rules.title: Prefer targeted operations
rules.operativeCondition: The agent can choose between broad and focused context operations.
rules.mechanism: Prefer many small targeted operations and keep the working set tidy as routine maintenance.
rules.consequence: Reduction avoids broad irreversible-looking guesses.
rules.evidence: Prefer many small targeted operations over one large blanket operation

rules.title: Memory guidance is feature-gated
rules.operativeCondition: The memory block is enabled and project-memory is injected.
rules.mechanism: Compose the memory instructions only when memory is enabled; omit them when disabled.
rules.consequence: The prompt does not advertise a memory surface that is unavailable.
rules.evidence: Gated out when `memory.enabled: false`

rules.title: Temporal boundary interpretation
rules.scope: primary sessions with temporal awareness enabled
rules.operativeCondition: Temporal HTML comments or session-history date attributes are present.
rules.mechanism: Use elapsed-time comments and start-date/end-date boundaries when reasoning about pacing and durations.
rules.consequence: Workflow timing is based on real session boundaries.
rules.evidence: Use these when reasoning about workflow pacing

rules.title: Caveman compression is not a style
rules.scope: primary sessions with caveman compression enabled
rules.operativeCondition: Older compressed text uses terse caveman style.
rules.mechanism: Write new turns in normal prose and consciously revert if the output drifts.
rules.consequence: Compression artifacts do not become new assistant voice.
rules.evidence: DO NOT mimic this style in new turns

rules.title: Preserve structural language tokens
rules.scope: primary sessions with a configured language
rules.operativeCondition: A primary reply language is configured.
rules.mechanism: Use the requested language for natural prose while keeping code, identifiers, paths, commands, logs, and quoted text verbatim.
rules.consequence: Localized prose cannot corrupt machine-readable or source-identifying text.
rules.evidence: Keep code, identifiers, file paths, commands, logs, and quoted text verbatim

rules.title: Subagents receive only bounded reduction mechanics
rules.operativeCondition: The session is a bounded single-task subagent with ctx_reduce.
rules.mechanism: Compose the marker, tag range syntax, protected tail, silent reduction, no blanket drops, and real-tool requirement without primary partner, memory, note, or search curation.
rules.consequence: A subagent gets the mechanics it can observe without primary-session obligations.
rules.evidence: Minimal guidance for SUBAGENT sessions

rules.title: Subagent dropped-sentinel asymmetry
rules.operativeCondition: Older tool calls appear as `[dropped §N§]` sentinels in a subagent context.
rules.mechanism: Treat sentinels as normal context management, never as a pattern to copy; make a fresh real tool call and never fabricate or inline its output.
rules.consequence: The dropped placeholder cannot be imitated as assistant content.
rules.evidence: sentinels; that is normal context management, not a pattern to copy.
rules.asymmetry: This exact sentinel-imitation clause is present in SUBAGENT_REDUCE_INTRO and not in BASE_INTRO; the checklist intentionally keeps its primary rows not-present.

rules.title: Subagents retain user and assistant text
rules.operativeCondition: A subagent chooses content to drop.
rules.mechanism: Drop only large tool outputs; do not drop user or assistant text messages.
rules.consequence: The child task keeps its instructions and conversational reasoning.
rules.evidence: Do not drop user or assistant text messages

rules.title: Subagents review ranges before dropping
rules.operativeCondition: A large tag range is under consideration.
rules.mechanism: Review each tag before selecting a drop range; never drop a large range blindly.
rules.consequence: The bounded child does not discard mixed-value evidence by shortcut.
rules.evidence: NEVER drop large ranges blindly

rules.title: Reduction prompts are housekeeping, not scarcity
rules.operativeCondition: Context usage or a reduction prompt is visible.
rules.mechanism: Treat reduction as routine maintenance and never reduce task scope or depth because context is large.
rules.consequence: Cache maintenance cannot cause the agent to rush, defer, or omit work.
rules.evidence: never let context size change *what* work you take on or *how thoroughly*

rules.title: No-reduce sessions are automatically managed
rules.operativeCondition: The reduction tool is unavailable.
rules.mechanism: Rely on automatic context management; do not prune, heed reduction warnings, or cut task scope or depth.
rules.consequence: An unavailable reduction tool cannot create false manual housekeeping obligations.
rules.evidence: there's nothing to prune and no warnings to act on

rules.title: No-reduce sessions retain recovery guidance without pruning instructions
rules.operativeCondition: Prior project or compacted-session context is needed while ctx_reduce is unavailable.
rules.mechanism: Keep note, memory, search, expansion, and real-tool guidance while omitting tag and reduction mechanics.
rules.consequence: The agent can recover hidden context without being told to call an unavailable tool.
rules.evidence: when ctx_reduce is unavailable

rules.title: ctx_reduce queues release
rules.operativeCondition: A spent tagged output should leave the working set.
rules.mechanism: Mark it discardable; release is queued and delayed until context space is needed.
rules.consequence: The original remains visible until the system releases it.
rules.evidence: Marking QUEUES content for release

rules.title: ctx_reduce protects newest tags
rules.operativeCondition: A requested tag is in the recent window.
rules.mechanism: The newest tags are protected and age out before release.
rules.consequence: Marking recent output is harmless.
rules.evidence: The newest tags are protected

rules.title: ctx_reduce recovery is explicit
rules.operativeCondition: Content has finally been released.
rules.mechanism: It becomes a short placeholder; rerun the recovery tool to get it back, and mark only content that is genuinely done.
rules.consequence: The agent does not treat an unrecovered output as safely disposable.
rules.evidence: re-running the tool is the only way to get it back

rules.title: ctx_reduce eligible output boundary
rules.operativeCondition: Choosing output to mark.
rules.mechanism: Prefer summarized, repeated, redundant, persisted, or merely confirmatory status output; keep user messages, unresolved errors, raw evidence, and exact wording that matters.
rules.consequence: Reduction preserves unresolved and authoritative evidence.
rules.evidence: Keep: user messages, unresolved errors, raw evidence you haven't extracted yet

rules.title: ctx_reduce rejects blind ranges
rules.operativeCondition: A large range is under consideration.
rules.mechanism: Review every tag before calling the drop parameter.
rules.consequence: A blanket range cannot silently discard mixed-value content.
rules.evidence: Never blanket-mark large ranges

rules.title: ctx_expand uses compacted headings
rules.operativeCondition: A summary under session-history lacks required detail.
rules.mechanism: Pass the heading's start/end ordinal range to recover the original conversation.
rules.consequence: Exact historical context can be restored from the summary boundary.
rules.evidence: expand the range

rules.title: ctx_expand has a bounded range result
rules.operativeCondition: The requested transcript exceeds the recovery budget.
rules.mechanism: Return a raw transcript capped at about 15K tokens and identify where to continue.
rules.consequence: The agent can continue recovery without receiving an unbounded result.
rules.evidence: capped at ~15K tokens; an oversized range returns the head

rules.title: ctx_expand verbose mode identifies parts
rules.operativeCondition: The agent needs to choose one message or tool call from a range.
rules.mechanism: Use verbose mode to list each message ordinal separately with per-part previews and tool output sizes.
rules.consequence: The agent can select a precise ordinal before full recovery.
rules.evidence: lists each message SEPARATELY with its ordinal

rules.title: ctx_expand ordinal mode recovers one message
rules.operativeCondition: One exact message or dropped tool output is needed.
rules.mechanism: Pass message=N to return all text parts and complete tool input/output for that ordinal.
rules.consequence: A previously dropped output is recovered from storage rather than fabricated.
rules.evidence: returns the FULL untruncated content of the message

rules.title: ctx_expand does not reread the live tail
rules.operativeCondition: A requested range is after the last compacted compartment.
rules.mechanism: Treat that range as already visible live context and do not expand it.
rules.consequence: The tool does not duplicate visible content and burn output tokens.
rules.evidence: Ranges after the last compartment are your live tail

rules.title: ctx_note action contract
rules.operativeCondition: The agent has a future session concern.
rules.mechanism: write saves, read lists, update changes, and dismiss retires notes; smart notes use surface_condition.
rules.consequence: Each note action has an explicit lifecycle operation.
rules.evidence: Actions:

rules.title: ctx_note smart conditions are external-only
rules.operativeCondition: A smart note is requested.
rules.mechanism: Use only externally verifiable signals from GitHub, disk, git history, or web pages; never a condition that depends on this conversation or an unobservable future action.
rules.consequence: The background checker can evaluate the condition without conversation access.
rules.evidence: using ONLY externally verifiable signals

rules.title: ctx_memory stores durable project claims
rules.operativeCondition: A fact must survive this session.
rules.mechanism: Create one durable project claim with category and content.
rules.consequence: Future sessions can use the memory without reconstructing this conversation.
rules.evidence: create a claim (content + category)

rules.title: ctx_memory action and privilege boundary
rules.operativeCondition: A memory must be changed or fetched.
rules.mechanism: Use create, get, revise, archive, restore, or merge; list remains dreamer-only.
rules.consequence: Primary agents cannot assume the dreamer-only list action is available.
rules.evidence: list: enumerate visible active claims (dreamer maintenance only)

rules.title: ctx_search returns only hidden history
rules.operativeCondition: The agent needs project recall.
rules.mechanism: Search memories, compacted messages, git commits, and notes while filtering memories already rendered in project-memory and the live conversation tail.
rules.consequence: Search fills missing context rather than duplicating visible context.
rules.evidence: Results only contain things you CANNOT currently see

rules.title: ctx_memory identity and mutation boundary
rules.operativeCondition: A known claim must be fetched or changed.
rules.mechanism: Use get with opaque public IDs and the current mutation token for changes; list remains dreamer-only.
rules.consequence: Primary agents use canonical claim identities and cannot assume dreamer browsing privileges.
rules.evidence: Reuse the exact token returned by create/get/list

rules.title: ctx_search source routing and ID lookup
rules.operativeCondition: A recall query needs a source boundary or direct memory lookup.
rules.mechanism: Omit sources for broad search, select memory/message/git_commit/note sources for targeted retrieval, or pass memory IDs to bypass text search; message hits continue through ctx_expand.
rules.consequence: Search scope and exact-memory lookup are explicit rather than guessed.
